text:
There's no single best one, because it depends on how much power you need. Here are the picks I'd look at, based on these search results.

**Best value: BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 with 200W panel, $699** (list $999)
- It has 1,024 Wh, 1,800 W AC output (3,600 W surge) and a 10 ms UPS, and charges 0-80% in about 45 minutes. It has 4.5 stars across 1.8k reviews.
- That's enough for a fridge, CPAP or power tools in an outage, plus camping.
- [Amazon listing](https://www.amazon.com/solar-generator-panels/s?k=solar+generator+with+solar+panels)

**Best all-rounder: Jackery Solar Generator 1000 v2**
- Talk of the House named it their editor's choice: 1,070 Wh, 1,500 W output, 1-hour fast charge, 23.8 lbs. The result didn't show a price, so check it before buying.
- [Review and price links](https://www.talkofthehouse.com/best-solar-generator-kits-with-panels/)

**Expandable option: EcoFlow Delta 2 with 220W panel**
- It has 1,024 Wh, 1,800 W output and 15 outlets, and expands to 3 kWh. Talk of the House called it best value. Top Consumer Reviews also ranked EcoFlow first overall for its app, deals and UPS function.
- [Talk of the House](https://www.talkofthehouse.com/best-solar-generator-kits-with-panels/) · [Top Consumer Reviews](https://www.topconsumerreviews.com/best-solar-generators/detailed-reviews.php)

**For serious home backup**
- **BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 with 2x200W panels, $1,399:** 2,073.6 Wh and 2,600 W output. [Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/solar-generator-panels/s?k=solar+generator+with+solar+panels)
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 kit:** 2,042 Wh and 2,200 W output. Talk of the House picked it for home backup. [Review](https://www.talkofthehouse.com/best-solar-generator-kits-with-panels/)

**If you shop at Costco:** the Jackery Explorer 1500 v2 with a solar panel is $899.99 online. It was out of stock at the Mountain View warehouse, but delivery was available. [Costco](https://www.costco.com/home-solar-power.html)

**Things to watch for**
- **ALLPOWERS P1800 (1,024 Wh):** it's about $395 with code ALLPOWERS26, but the listing doesn't say a panel is included. You'd have to buy panels separately. It also has a shorter 24-month warranty. [Dealectric listing](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-p1800-1024wh) (an affiliate link, per the site).
- **Cheap 300W units on Walmart:** many no-name units cost $120-$180 and include a small panel. They're fine for phones and lights, but not for appliances.
- **Check the panel wattage:** a 200W panel takes roughly 5-6 hours of good sun to refill a 1 kWh battery, so bigger panels charge much faster.
- **Review sources:** the review sites earn commissions on links, so treat their rankings as one input.

If you tell me your budget and what you want to power (camping gear, a fridge, a whole house), I can narrow this to one pick.
